name: A Disjoint Passive Shore Forces an Acquired Terminal Square
statement: In the active--passive normalization, suppose the active slice is the singleton $L=\{a\}$ and a passive shore $S_z$ is disjoint from every other passive shore. If $S_z$ contains an active edge $xy$ of direction $f$, then $\{z,f\}\in\operatorname{Sh}(A)\setminus\operatorname{Sh}(K)$. Thus the terminal square over that shore edge is genuinely acquired by the upper family, regardless of other vertices of $K$.
proof: The vertices $x,y,x^{\oplus z},y^{\oplus z}$ form a full $\{z,f\}$-square in $A$. If $K$ also shattered this pair, ampleness would give a second full square in $K$. The anchors of all such squares form a connected ample carrier, so an anchor path joins the displayed split square to the square in $K$. The first step changing another passive coordinate $w$ starts from a square whose base-layer side contains two vertices; since $L$ is a singleton, one is a lower concept $d$. The adjacent squares then put both $d^{\oplus z}$ and $d^{\oplus w}$ in $K$, implying $d\in S_z\cap S_w$, contrary to shore disjointness.
